Q: SQL - left join generate duplicates A:

Use GROUP BY

to avoid duplicates. In your case:

...
    WHERE 
        a.closed='N' 
    AND 
        a.paid = 'N' 
    GROUP BY
        a.id
    ORDER BY 
        a.arrived_date 
    DESC

Q: Online MariaDB Server can't be accessed outside of MariaDB command Line A:

The error Access denied for user 'user'@'password' means your PHP code is passing the password where the host belongs. You can see the host part of the error is literally your password. The MariaDB CLI works because you're probably typing the flags in the right order there.

Just swap the arguments so they match what mysqli_connect expects:

$conn = mysqli_connect('hostname', 'user', 'your_actual_password', 'database');

I'd check your HeidiSQL settings too. It's likely the same issue where a field is swapped or misplaced. But the error string is the dead giveaway here.

Q: Removing "semi" duplicates on an inner join in mySQL A:

I've figured that the best solution to this issue is to order the data set, following suggestion by @Strawberry and operate on this by grouping each ID and parent ID pair, selecting the minimum ordered value for each, setting that as a new field for each group and then deleting all rows for which the ordered value and minimum value are not equal.
